requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in woodwork activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. Explain what precautions you should take to safely use your tools. (b) Show that you know first aid for injuries that could occur while woodworking, including splinters, scratches, cuts, severe bleeding, and shock. Tell what precautions must be taken to help prevent loss of eyesight or hearing, and explain why and when it is necessary to use a dust mask. (c) Earn the Totin' Chip recognition.

pamphlet_excerpts: Then Workers Buckers: Then workers called buckers lop off the limbs and slice thetrunks into shorter lengths (logs) that are easier to handle.
Logs Trucked Floated: The logs are trucked, floated, or carried on railroads to asawmill.
Mill Logs Debarked: At the mill, logs are debarked (their bark is removed), and saws cut them into boards (lumber).
Small Logs Cut: Small logs are often cut into boards in a single pass through a set of saws (a gang saw) that makes many cuts at once.
step_by_step_procedure: Largelogs Several Passes: Largelogs may make several passes through one saw (a headsaw) thatslices off a board at a time until the whole log is cut into lumber.
New Lumber Green: The new lumber, called green lumber, is edged and trimmed tostraighten the sides and cut into boards of standard lengths.
Lumber Graded Quality: Lumber is graded for quality, appearance, and strength.
Manufacturersuse Them Tomake: Manufacturersuse them tomake flooring, pallets, andsimilar products.

pamphlet_excerpts: Likely Mar Work: You are more likely to mar your work and injureyourself with a dull blade than a sharp one because dull bladesrequire extra force and can slip.
Rough Handling will Nick: Rough handling will nick and dull the cutting edges.
Wood-cutting Tools: Most wood-cutting tools have two wedgeshapes on their cutting edge: the main or groundbevel, and the sharpening bevel.
Aresharpening Edge Working: When you aresharpening an edge, you should be working off thesharpening bevel only, not the larger ground bevel.
step_by_step_procedure: Start Roughstone Followed: When sharpening a blade, start with a roughstone, followed by (in this order and as needed) a medium, fine, and smooth stone.
Whet Edge Pushing: Whet the edge by pushing itforward over the stone.
Finish Turn Blade: To finish, turn the blade over on Correct angle for sharpening the cuttingits flat side and, keeping the back flatiron of a planeon the stone, push it.
Stoningboth Sides Produces: Stoningboth sides produces a little wiry burron the edge.

pamphlet_excerpts: Mortise Tenon Joint: A mortise and tenon joint has twoparts: the mortise is a hole in one pieceof wood, and the tenon is the part ofthe second piece that is cut and shapedto.
Simply Jointis Square: Simply, this jointis “a square peg in a square hole.” To start the mortise, drill the holesonly as deep as you want the mortiseto be.
Then Sharp Wood: Then use a sharp wood chisel toshave out any excess wood and squarethe corners.
Markits Depth Width: To make the tenon, markits depth and width on the end of thetenon piece.
step_by_step_procedure: Backsaw Cut Thetenon: Use a backsaw to cut thetenon, making a series of straight, square cuts to remove excess wood.
Think Tenant Someone: Think of “tenant”, someone whodwells inside a place, to help you remember that the tenon (the peg) goes inside the mortise (the hole).

pamphlet_excerpts: Mortise Tenon Joint: A mortise and tenon joint has twoparts: the mortise is a hole in one pieceof wood, and the tenon is the part ofthe second piece that is cut and shapedto.
Simply Jointis Square: Simply, this jointis “a square peg in a square hole.” To start the mortise, drill the holesonly as deep as you want the mortiseto be.
Then Sharp Wood: Then use a sharp wood chisel toshave out any excess wood and squarethe corners.
Markits Depth Width: To make the tenon, markits depth and width on the end of thetenon piece.
step_by_step_procedure: Backsaw Cut Thetenon: Use a backsaw to cut thetenon, making a series of straight, square cuts to remove excess wood.
Think Tenant Someone: Think of “tenant”, someone whodwells inside a place, to help you remember that the tenon (the peg) goes inside the mortise (the hole).
Requirement Choose Aproject: For requirement 6, you might choose aproject below, take an idea from a bookor website listed in the resources section, or think.
Optional Requirement: For optional requirement 6(e), your merit badge counselor or Scoutmaster may suggest a Good Turn that you and your buddies can do.
